stations.name: Mystery Food
stations.short: Investigate food using more than one sense.
stations.question: You are eating a fruit. Which sense organs can work together to help you notice its color, smell, and taste?
stations.clue: Your eyes see the food, your nose smells it, and your tongue tastes it.

stations.name: Read & Listen
stations.short: See words and hear a reader.
stations.question: A teacher reads a story while you look at the book. Which sense organs work together?
stations.clue: Your eyes see the words and pictures. Your ears hear the teacher's voice.

stations.name: Touch Detective
stations.short: Discover an object by feeling it.
stations.question: You place your hand on a covered object and feel that it is rough. Which sense organ gives you this touch information?
stations.clue: The skin helps you feel textures such as rough and smooth. In the real activity, use safe objects.

stations.name: Sound Detective
stations.short: Listen and connect the sound to what you see.
stations.question: You see a musical instrument and hear its sound. Which sense organs work together?
stations.clue: Your eyes help you see the instrument, while your ears hear the sound.

stations.name: Safety Mission
stations.short: Use your senses to stay safe.
stations.question: When crossing a street, which two sense organs work together to help you notice vehicles?
stations.clue: Your eyes see vehicles and your ears hear vehicle sounds. These warning signals can help keep you safe.
